layout.heading: Page Layout — Presets, Cells & Lines
layout.body: Click Layout Settings under the View & Layout tab to open page settings. Use quick presets: 8.5×11in (US Letter, 32 × 25 cells) or 11×11.5in (wide tractor paper, 40 × 25), or choose Custom and set Cells / row (10–100) and Lines / page (5–50) yourself—for example 28 lines for A4-style pages. These values drive the on-screen preview, the downloaded .brf, and are saved for your next visit.
layout.viewPlusNote: ViewPlus embossers: Under Layout Settings you can tune left padding (extra blank cells per line) for US Letter. Padding is applied when printing only if your layout is US Letter (8.5×11 preset or 32 × 25). Single-sheet alignment varies by model; if you dial in a value that works for your paper and want to share it, email grahamthetvi@icloud.com. When you use Print with a ViewPlus driver, a short reminder appears there too.

embossing.heading: Seamless Embossing (WebUSB & Bridge)
embossing.body: The app includes embosser drivers for Enabling Technologies, Index, ViewPlus, Braillo, and others—pick the model that matches your device when you print. ChromeOS users can use WebUSB to send braille directly from the browser. Windows/macOS/Linux users run the small Graham Bridge app so print jobs reach the embosser reliably. ViewPlus left-margin tuning stays under Layout Settings (see above). By default the bridge listens only on 127.0.0.1:8080 and accepts browser traffic from official Graham Braille Editor sites (and local dev). Optional Share mode lets another Bridge on your LAN send jobs (paired with a short code).

linux.heading: Linux Bridge
steps: ZIP: move graham-bridge-linux-amd64 to /usr/local/bin/graham-bridge, install the .desktop file, launch from the app menu
Fedora / RPM: from Releases, download graham-bridge-<version>-linux-fedora.x86_64.rpm, then sudo dnf install ./that-file.rpm

sharedPi.heading: Shared Bridge (Pi or desktop)
steps: Option A — Dedicated Raspberry Pi: install the linux-arm64 Bridge on Raspberry Pi OS Desktop, set up the embosser in CUPS, then Bridge → Settings → Share on this network → set a name → note the code and the Pi’s IP
Option B — Existing embosser PC (Windows/macOS/Linux): on the machine already connected to the embosser, open Bridge → Settings → Share on this network → set a name → note the code and that PC’s IP
On each teacher PC: install Bridge → Settings → Connect to a shared Bridge → enter the share host’s IP and code
In the editor, print as usual and choose the shared embosser in the printer list
sharedPi.itNote: IT: devices must be allowed to talk on the LAN (disable client isolation or use a print VLAN). Reserve a static IP or DNS name for the share host. Allow TCP port 8081 to the host. On Windows share hosts, allow inbound TCP 8081 in Windows Defender Firewall (or ask IT) if pairing fails.

remoteInbox.heading: Remote inbox (rclone + Email BRF)
steps: Senders still use Email BRF (Export → Email BRF, attach the downloaded .brf) or place that .brf in a shared Google Drive folder such as Graham Embosser Inbox
On the embosser computer, create a local folder (for example GrahamInbox in your home directory) and install rclone from rclone.org
Run rclone config, add a Google Drive remote named gdrive (school account), then rclone move that Drive folder into GrahamInbox on a timer — do not use rclone sync
Bridge → Settings → Inbox folder → set the local path, choose the embosser, Save. New .brf files print automatically and move to printed/
remoteInbox.itNote: Graham never logs into Drive. rclone uses the school Google account. Windows may use Google Drive for desktop instead of rclone, watching the same local folder. Full commands are in Bridge Settings.

math.heading: Math Translation — LaTeX to Braille
math.body: The editor auto-detects LaTeX math in your text and translates it to braille math notation. Wrap display (block) equations in $$…$$ (translated to Nemeth) and inline expressions in \(…\) (translated to UEB Math).
math.tip: Tip: For best results, paste your document into an AI assistant (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, etc.) with the following request before pasting it here:
math.promptText: "Please reformat my text so that every mathematical expression, equation, and arithmetic operation — including plain numbers used in a math context — is wrapped in LaTeX notation: \(…\) for inline math and $$…$$ for display equations. Leave all non-math prose unchanged."

downloading.heading: Downloading & Autosave
downloading.body: When your translation is ready, click Download BRF under the File tab to output standard .brf files formatted directly to your selected page layout settings. For print-over-braille, click Download print layout to get an .rtf sized to your paper: each print line has the same words as that braille line, in one font size. Print the sheet, then emboss the BRF on the same paper.
downloading.autosave: Your work is automatically saved as you type. Click Drafts under the File tab to view and restore unsaved work from the last 30 days.

perkins.heading: Perkins Viewer
perkins.body: Click Perkins Viewer under the Teaching Tools tab to practice or demo 6-key Perkins entry directly in your browser. This mode overlays on the right panel, giving a dedicated interactive simulator for standard brailler practice without disrupting your primary document.

largePrint.heading: Large-Print (Jumbo) Braille
largePrint.body: For dual-media print/braille books or low-vision readers, you can insert large-print sections. Click Large Print under the Teaching Tools tab to configure size and insert blocks. In the right-hand preview panel, these blocks are translated and rendered as large-print Braille cells in BRF format, preserving tactile readability and alignment.

music.heading: Music Braille
music.body: Graham does not yet convert sheet music into Music Braille automatically. For Music Braille, open Music Player Mode under Teaching Tools or Music Braille Guide under Help & Support. We recommend creating or exporting MusicXML in MuseScore, converting it with Sao Mai Braille (SMB desktop or online), then optionally importing the .brf here to preview or emboss. You can also Add to translation page so the instructions themselves can be embossed as braille.

graphics.heading: Tactile Graphics & 3D Printing
graphics.body: Use the Graphics tab buttons — Math, Shapes, Drawing, and Door Sign (STL) — to open tactile tools or export a 3D door sign. Tactile Design lets you draw freehand, place Shape Inventory stamps with size and fill controls, and add braille labels on the same canvas for diagrams (for example, a flower with labeled parts).
graphics.simpleShapes: Simple Shapes: Lines, rectangles, and adjustable polygons.
graphics.complexShapes: Complex Shapes: Cloud, Crescent Moon, Lightning Bolt, 5-Pointed Star, Apple, and Cross. Shapes like the Cross support adjusting the width/height of the bars directly.
graphics.positioningTool: Canvas tools: Use the pointer to select and move braille labels and stamped shapes; pencil, line, Shape Inventory, and braille label tools build the diagram.
graphics.customElements: Custom Elements: Includes details like a Paintbrush, Flower/Daisy blooms (always rendered with filled centers for contrast), and Vampire Fangs.
graphics.dotPatternPreview: Dot Pattern Preview: The editor displays canvas shapes as physical Braille dot grids in real-time.
graphics.stlNote: Additionally, click Door Sign (STL) under the Graphics tab to export your paginated braille layout as a 3D-printable STL file with standard BANA midpoint dot spacing.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy (TL;DR)
privacy.intro: At Graham Braille Editor, your privacy and data security are our top priorities. Because of the sensitive nature of the documents you may be translating, we've designed this app to process everything locally.
privacy.tldrLead: Here is the TL;DR of how we handle your data:

tldr.localProcessing: 100% Local Processing: All braille translation, text processing, and 3D STL generation happens directly inside your web browser. Your documents never leave your device.
tldr.noCloudServers: No Cloud Servers: We do not upload your text, braille files, or any personal information to any cloud servers.
tldr.localStorageOnly: Local Storage Only: Your drafts, application settings, and table preferences are saved securely within your browser's local storage.
tldr.offlineCapable: Offline Capable: Once the web page is loaded, the core translation features work completely offline.
tldr.embosserBridge: Embosser Bridge: If you use our local printing bridge application, your files are transmitted directly to your local embosser over your own computer/network, not over the internet. Optional Share mode accepts print jobs from other Graham Bridges on your LAN that know your share code—still with no cloud relay.
tldr.emailBrf: Email BRF: If you use Email BRF, Graham downloads the .brf to your computer and opens Gmail compose in your browser. Graham does not send the email, attach the file, or upload the document. You attach and send from your own Gmail account.
tldr.inboxFolder: Inbox folder: Optional Bridge inbox printing reads .brf files from a folder on the embosser computer (often filled by rclone or Drive for desktop). Graham does not access Google Drive; your school’s account and tools do.
tldr.noTracking: No Tracking: We do not use analytics, trackers, or advertising cookies. What you do in the editor is entirely your business.

fullPolicy.intro: At Graham Braille Editor, we believe that your data is yours alone. Because our software is used to translate sensitive educational, personal, and professional documents, we have built our architecture around the principle of strict local-first processing. This Privacy Policy details exactly how your information is handled when you use our application.

section1.heading: 1. Information We Do Not Collect
section1.lead: We do not collect, transmit, or store any personal information, documents, or usage data.
section1.noAnalytics: No Analytics: We do not use Google Analytics, tracking pixels, or any other telemetry to monitor your behavior.
section1.noAccounts: No Accounts: You are not required to create an account, provide an email address, or log in to use the editor.
section1.noCloudStorage: No Cloud Storage: We do not upload your text, translated braille, imported files, or exported STLs to any server.
section1.emailBrf: Email BRF: Choosing Email BRF only downloads the file locally and opens Gmail compose in your browser. Graham does not send mail or transmit the braille file; you attach it yourself from Downloads.

section2.heading: 2. How Your Data is Processed (Client-Side Only)
section2.body: All core functionality of the Graham Braille Editor happens directly inside your web browser. When you type text, translate it to braille, or generate a 3D printable STL file, the computation is performed entirely by your device's processor using web technologies. Because the processing is local, your documents never leave your computer.

section3.heading: 3. Local Storage
section3.lead: To provide a seamless experience, we save certain data locally on your device using your browser's standard localStorage and IndexedDB capabilities. This includes:
section3.appSettings: Application Settings: Your selected braille tables, theme preferences (dark/light mode), and page layout configurations.
section3.autosavedDrafts: Autosaved Drafts: The text you are currently working on is periodically saved locally so that you do not lose your work if you accidentally close the tab. You can clear this data at any time by clearing your browser's site data or by using the "Discard All" functionality within the editor's Drafts menu.

section4.heading: 4. Graham Bridge Application (Optional)
section4.lead: If you choose to use the Graham Bridge desktop application to send print jobs to your local embosser, please note:
section4.localServer: By default the bridge runs a local server on your machine (binding only to 127.0.0.1) for the web editor. If you enable Share mode, it also listens on your LAN (port 8081) for authenticated jobs from other Graham Bridges that pair with your share code. There is no cloud relay.
section4.facilitates: It facilitates communication exclusively between your web browser (via the local Bridge) and your local or paired shared embosser.
section4.noInternet: The bridge application does not upload your documents to Graham cloud servers. Optional Share mode stays on your LAN and requires the shared code to pair.
section4.shareMode: Anyone on your local network who knows the current share code can pair and send embosser jobs until you regenerate the code or turn Share off.
section4.inboxFolder: Optional inbox folder: if enabled, Bridge prints .brf files that appear in a local folder you choose. rclone or Google Drive for desktop may copy school Drive files into that folder; Graham does not receive those files on our servers.

section5.heading: 5. Third-Party Hosting
section5.body: The Graham Braille Editor is delivered to your browser via standard web hosting (such as GitHub Pages). When you visit the site to load the application, the hosting provider may collect standard server logs (such as your IP address and user agent) as part of their standard operational procedures. However, the Graham Braille Editor application itself injects no third-party tracking scripts.

section6.heading: 6. Children's Privacy and Educational Use
section6.body: Because our application does not collect, store, or transmit personal data, it is inherently compliant with children's privacy regulations such as COPPA (Children's Online Privacy Protection Act) and FERPA (Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act). It is safe for use in classrooms and by students of all ages.

section7.heading: 7. Changes to this Policy
section7.body: We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. Any changes will be reflected in this document within the application. Because we do not collect your contact information, we cannot notify you of changes via email.

section8.heading: 8. Contact Information
section8.body: If you have any questions or concerns about this Privacy Policy or how your data is handled, please contact us at: grahamthetvi@icloud.com

stlExport.title: 3D Door Sign (STL)
stlExport.description: Uses BANA midpoint dimensions (mm): dot diameter, height, intra-cell, inter-cell, and line spacing. The STL is exported standing upright (Z axis is the sign height, Y is the thickness) for optimal 3D print quality. When exporting exactly one line of text, an ADA-style large print label is generated above the braille (or to the right of any optional logo). Because standing a thin plate upright can be unstable during printing, we highly recommend enabling a brim or raft in your slicer.

chart.title: Data-to-Braille Chart Generator
chart.stepAnnouncement: Step {{current}} of 4: {{stepName}}. Chart graphics use low-resolution 6-dot cells; a plain-text summary is inserted with each chart so exact values stay available for reading and embossing.

dataStep.xValuesHint: If provided, must have the same count as Y. Empty uses 0, 1, 2, … in order.
dataStep.pasteHint: Optional: paste CSV — one Y per line, or two columns (X, Y) per line

chartTypeStep.mathDescription: Applies when the editor translates $$…$$ and \(…\). This choice is saved for the app and used for the whole document. With Nemeth, numeric lines use $$…$$ blocks (kind and title stay literary), and a form feed places the graphic on the following page; with UEB math, the summary stays plain prose above the chart on the same page sequence.
chartTypeStep.nemeth: Nemeth — US math notation (often wrapped for UEB literary context)
chartTypeStep.uebMath: UEB math — Unified English Braille math

reviewStep.heading: Review — text summary to insert
reviewStep.nemethNote: Nemeth layout below: kind and title lines are literary; grid, range, axes, and each value pair use $$…$$. The chart starts on the next page after a form feed. LaTeX math elsewhere uses Nemeth (set on step 2).
reviewStep.uebNote: Plain English below will appear above the tactile chart and will be translated with your literary table like the rest of the document. LaTeX math in the file uses UEB math (set on step 2).
reviewStep.fixDataHint: Fix data on step 1 before inserting.
